AI Boom Propels Samsung to Record 2Q26 Results as Operating Profit Surges 1,814% YoY  Samsung Electronics reported record-breaking results for the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure. The company posted consolidated revenue of ₩171.5T, up 130% YoY, while operating profit reached ₩89.5T, soaring 1,814% YoY. Both figures marked new quarterly records.. According to Samsung's financial results, the exceptional performance was driven almost entirely by the company's semiconductor business, underscoring the strong profitability of AI-related memory products.   hashtag #HBM4 and AIServer Demand Drive Semiconductor Growth  Samsung's Device Solutions (DS) division, which oversees its semiconductor operations, generated ₩127.5T in revenue and ₩89.2T in operating profit during the quarter.  According to the company's 2Q26 earnings presentation, the Memory Business recorded ₩120.8T in revenue, representing a 471% YoY increase and setting a new all-time high.  Samsung stated that, amid tight production capacity, it prioritized shipments to the server market, where continued memory price increases helped server products account for a record share of memory revenue. The company also significantly expanded shipments of HBM4 and delivered samples of the industry's first HBM4E to major customers, further reinforcing its technology leadership in next-generation AI memory.  In addition, Samsung's foundry business reported improved profitability, supported by strong orders from U.S. customers and growing demand for HBM base dies. The company also continued securing 2nm HPC design wins, strengthening its advanced foundry pipeline.   hashtag #Rising Component Costs Weighon Consumer Electronics  In contrast to the strong performance of the semiconductor business, Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division, which includes smartphones and consumer electronics, faced mounting cost pressures. Quarterly revenue declined 9% sequentially.  Within the DX division, the Mobile eXperience (MX) business reported ₩33.2T in revenue and an operating loss of ₩0.7T, primarily due to industry-wide increases in component costs that weighed on profitability.  TrendForce notes that while AI infrastructure investment continues to drive robust demand for high-value memory products such as HBM and server DRAM, rising component costs are increasingly pressuring consumer electronics manufacturers.
